coverageSpotVerification.detail:
coverage.json (sha256:51f44bd0…2814) maps assertions to milestones; the mapped test is that milestone's scripts/suite.mjs runner, which I re-ran green for m1-m6 and m8. Sampling the mappings against the runner's source and behaviour:
M1 — honest. Every one of the seven mapped assertions has a real assertion in runM1 that can fail.
M2 — dishonest. m2-a12 (URL renders as tappable text) and m2-a13 (no preview card) have no assertion anywhere in the suite: runM2 creates a post whose body contains a URL and never inspects rendering. m2-a18 (a repost by a followed user surfaces the original in Following) is never tested. m2-a22 (Following-tab pagination on scroll) is never tested; the only pagination assertion is `page1.data.length <= 20` on the Global tab, and I independently found both feed tabs do not page at all. m2-a25's mapped assertion is `assert.ok(own.some(row => row.post?.author && String(row.post.author).length > 0))`, which passes for any row with any author and cannot detect the implicit-self-follow behaviour it is mapped to. m2-a26 and m2-a27 are never tested.
M3 — dishonest. m3-a11 (tapping the quoted excerpt jumps to the original) is mapped, but the suite only asserts that the quoting mutation committed; it never touches the jump. I independently found the jump is broken.
M4 — dishonest. m4-a07 (re-tapping the emoji removes the reaction) is mapped to `assert.equal(true, true, "m4-a07 react remove")` — a tautology that cannot fail. m4-a06's replacement semantics and m4-a09's 'edited' label are likewise executed but never asserted.
M5 — dishonest. m5-a10 is mapped to `assert.ok((chat.data ?? []).length >= 0)` and m5-a11 to `assert.ok((all.data ?? []).length >= 0)`; both are vacuously true and would pass against an empty or broken search.
M6 — dishonest. m6-a10 and m6-a11 assert that scripts/custom-client-demo.mjs runs green and exercises every documented operation, but the suite never invokes that script. m6-a09 (view-once previews as 'Photo') is never tested. m6-a08's mapped check is `assert.ok(pushes.state === 'complete' || 'capped' || 'denied')`, which accepts a denial and inspects no payload field.
M7 — dishonest. Six M7 assertions are mapped, but scripts/suite.mjs has no m7 runner at all: `npm run acceptance -- --milestone m7` exits 1 with "no suite for m7".
M8 — dishonest. m8-a03, m8-a04, m8-a06 and m8-a07 have no assertion in runM8. m8-a05's mapped check is `assert.ok(trend.state === 'complete' || 'capped')` with no ranking check; m8-a01's is `typeof insights.data.posts === 'number'` with no comparison to seeded content.
Per the frozen grader prompt each dishonest milestone adjudicates to capability-failure (scoring-only, non-retroactive) and its checklist scores as not passed in O1.

defects.summary: Warm-offline search returns nothing. With the network cut and the app's own sm-search-offline indicator rendered, searching a term present in already-synced history returned zero results; the held-log fallback (shared/log.ts searchHeld over deliveries.inboxLog's last 50 rows) yielded no hits even for a message that had just been rendered in the thread and that online search matched.

defects.summary: The web client caps a conversation at its 30 most recent messages and never pages history, so older messages are unreachable in the app and a quoted-reply excerpt silently disappears when the quoted message falls outside that window.

defects.summary: Any group member, not only an admin, can change a group's accent colour and background image: snapback/groups.q updateChat gates name, description and disappearing on membership+admin but applies `accent` and `background` on membership alone.

defects.summary: The digest sweep sets periodStart to the emission instant rather than an anchored period boundary, so digestEmissions' (principal, periodStart) uniqueness key can never collide and the documented per-period guard is inert; the only real limiter is zeroing the counters. config/digest.json's periodAnchorUtc is never read.
defects.evidence: trace.md §10.2; source: snapback/admin.q job digestSweep (`start = now`, `prior = digestEmissions[p.principal, start]`). Observed digest payload carried periodStart == at == 1788744210849.

O1.anchorsCited: Brief Scoring O1: '*30:* core features partially work; several checklist items fail. *60:* M1–M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap. *90:* every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts.' Placed below the ~30 anchor.
O1.justification: Full-run scope is M1-M8 and every milestone stays in the denominator. Green receipts exist only for M1 and M2 (receipts/m1.jsonl, receipts/m2.jsonl). M3's receipt records green=false, nonGreenCause=choreography-failed with four failed checks. M4, M5, M6 and M8 have suite artifacts but no choreography receipt at all, so none of them is green. M7 was never attempted (no m7 runner in scripts/suite.mjs). No native platform-proof exists: artifacts/m6/simulator/attempt.txt and artifacts/m8/simulator/attempt.txt both record 'no Clique .app installed in this lane'. Decisively, the coverage-manifest spot verification found dishonest mappings in M2-M8 (see coverageSpotVerification.detail), which per the frozen prompt adjudicates each of those milestones to capability-failure and scores its checklist as not passed; only M1's checklist is creditable, i.e. one of eight in-scope milestones. That is materially worse than the ~30 anchor's 'core features partially work; several checklist items fail'. For the record, and not as the score: on my independent execution alone, of the 101 M1-M7 assertions in the manifest 68 passed, 9 failed and 24 were not-run (15 of those because their choreography or simulator segment produced no artifact at all, 9 because M7 was never attempted); the M1-M2 surface in particular was solid.

O2.anchorsCited: Brief Scoring O2: '*30:* multiple high-severity defects in core flows. *60:* a few medium defects off the happy path. *90:* only cosmetic nits.' Placed at the ~30 anchor.
O2.justification: Four major defects beyond the checklist, three of them squarely in core flows: a DM created through the documented custom-client API is unopenable in the web client and shows a garbage chat title (d-01); warm-offline search returns nothing even with the app's own offline indicator showing (d-02); conversation history is capped at the last 30 messages with no paging, which also silently drops quoted-reply excerpts (d-03); and the push preview is caller-supplied rather than server-derived (d-04). Six further minor defects (d-05 non-admin group customisation, d-06 inconsistent insight counters, d-07 raw principal ids as sender names, d-08 silently-reassigned handles at signup, d-09 API.md gaps, d-10 an inert digest period guard) and one cosmetic (d-11).
